explainer.description:
The explainer used for interpreting the results of the model. This reference points to the method or
technique employed to provide human-readable explanations of the model’s outputs.
In this case, the explainer is related to the Sigmoid Weighted Residual method.

initKwargs.description:
If the {@link #explainer} is a native Python class, these kwargs will be used to initialize the explainer in
addition to a native model or its process function.

callKwargs.description:
Keyword arguments for an {@link #explainer}'s interpret function. If the {@link #explainer} is a function, then
the native model being interpreted, or its process function, will also be passed in.

actionRequirement.description:
The {@link Action.Requirement minimal action requirement} in which all MlInterpreter methods for the pipe will be executed,
except {@link #interpret}, which may be overwritten by the pipe's action requirement, if set @see MlCustomPipe.actionRequirement.

typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

title:
This type represents an {@link MlInterpreter} that interprets the outputs of machine learning models using
the Sigmoid Weighted Residual (SWRI) method. This method applies a sigmoid transformation to the weighted residuals
for better interpretation of risk scores or predictions. It helps in generating human-readable explanations
for the model’s output, especially in the context of reliability and risk assessment models.

The SWRI is useful in cases where risk scores need to be smoothed or transformed in a way that their relationship
with features can be better understood. It can provide insights into how much each feature contributes to the
final risk prediction after applying a weighted residual approach.
name: ReliabilityRiskMl.Pipeline.Interpreter.SigmoidWeightedResidualInterpreter
